set.v: About $7,000 cash in first reports (the $90,000 figure is from later accounts)
set.st: On October 20, 1931 the Holden-Keating gang robbed the Kraft State Bank in Menomonie of about $7,000 in first reports (later accounts say $90,000 with securities) and took hostages. They fled east on U.S. 12, north on County Trunk B, then east on old Suckow Road, spreading nails behind them. Days earlier they had stashed five-gallon gas cans at secluded abandoned farms so they could avoid towns. A wounded gang member was left dying at one of those abandoned farms with a handful of securities. Two robbers were caught in Kansas City eight months later. First reports (Sheboygan Press 20 Oct 1931) say about $7,000; the cashier's son was killed and his body left on the Wheeler road; one robber was convicted in Nov 1933. No paper 1931-35 says what became of the money, and none puts any of it hidden along the route. LiDAR cache check (USGS 1 m, 2018): Nothing that fits the story stands out within the search area: the pits and lines it finds there are ditches, banks, ponds or natural ground.
set.tovw: Lead grade D: documented 1931 robbery (period print read); no period source has loot hidden along the route; farms look-only
